title: Personality: Definition, Nature & Characteristics
summary: Personality defined as the dynamic organisation within the individual of those psychophysical systems that determine characteristic adjustments to the environment. Covers nature, characteristics, determinants and the person-situation debate.
objectives: Describe the nature and characteristics of personality.
Identify biological, environmental, psychological and situational determinants.
revision: Personality is the dynamic organisation of psychophysical systems determining characteristic adjustment. Determinants span biological, environmental, psychological and situational factors. Behaviour reflects person–situation interaction.
traps: Personality = dynamic organisation of psychophysical systems.

notes.t: The dynamic organisation within the individual of those psychophysical systems that determine the individual's characteristic adjustments to his environment (Allport, 1937).
Personality is relatively stable over time and across situations, yet allows for individual differences in how people think, feel and behave.

i: Consistency — recognisable patterns across time and contexts
Distinctiveness — individual differences make each person unique
Dynamic organisation — traits interact within a system
Psychophysical basis — rooted in biology and experience
Adjustment — determines how the person adapts to the environment
Environmental: family, culture, upbringing, life events

notes.t: Does behaviour flow from the person (traits) or the situation? Contemporary view: personality and situation interact — behaviour is a function of both the person and the environment.
UGC NET frequently asks for Allport's definition and the determinants of personality (biological, environmental, psychological, situational).

mnemonics.title: DYNAMIC
mnemonics.text: D — Dynamic organisation, Y — Yields consistency, N — Nature + nurture, A — Adjusts to environment, M — Makes each person unique, I — Integrates traits, C — Consistent across time

flashcards.a: Dynamic organisation of psychophysical systems determining characteristic adjustment.
